opti-1: Long ago, signs asked people to protect one rare Florida bird.
opti-2: The snail kite eats almost nothing but apple snails.
opti-3: And the snails? Look under the water.
opti-4: They eat this brown mat, called periphyton.
opti-5: Anhingas spear fish. Alligators eat fish, turtles, and birds.
opti-6: Every living thing here is connected.
opti-7: If one animal disappeared from the Everglades, what would happen to everything else?
29-02-welcome: Our film starts with a rare Florida bird and its favorite food. First, inspect a strange brown mat from the marsh.
29-02-lesson: Today you're an ecologist. Follow the Sun's energy to a snail kite, test which one makes its own food, then climb down the Energy Tower.
29-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
29-02-assign: Time to show what you learned. Sort the living things, then draw your own Everglades food web.
how-29-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the mat, then tap three things you notice.
how-29-02-compare: Put the sun lamp under one tray and the dish of algae under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-29-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-29-02-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name its role. Predict what happens if it disappears, and watch the real place appear.
how-29-02-partc: Draw a food web of the Everglades. Include at least 5 organisms and 6 arrows. Label each organism, and point each arrow the way the energy flows. Add a title.
